en: and apparently they let you see the outside
world while sitting in a theater. Unbelievable!
note: #3679-#3681: 'Lately there's a thing called moving pictures, / and apparently they let you see the outside / world while sitting in a theater. Unbelievable!'

en: Mind you, I haven't seen one myself yet.
They say you can see them if you go to London.
(London must be far more advanced
than I ever imagined...)
Glad I got to hear the rest. Thank you.
note: player, stern register; polite counterpart is #3712

en: Not at all.
What will become of this Public Hall?
note: player, stern register; polite counterpart is #3713

en: The building itself is behind the times,
so there's a proposal to make the most of
its charm and turn it into an "art museum."
However, buying up the artwork isn't going
well, so I think it will be a while yet
before the public can actually see it.
I'd like people to be able to use it
as a museum soon, but
the purchasing just isn't getting anywhere.
After all, without a fine collection of art,
we can't expect people to enjoy it.
No, I know where it is.
note: no speaker tag in msg 141194; read as the player declining directions to the Public Hall (cf. #3606)

en: Thank you very much.
Then why is it that you work here?
note: player, polite register; stern versions #3634/#3642 in slice 045

en: May I ask why
no one is using this Public Hall?
(What a cutting remark...)
note: player aside reacting to Josef's needling 'So, what "question" is it today?' (#3662)

en: I see, so that's how it came to be.
There's more to the story...
Oh, no, that's quite enough, thanks.
(Could it be that
is heading for London just to see
moving pictures?)
I'm so glad I got to hear the rest. Thank you.
What are your plans for this Public Hall?
Who is it?
What brings you here...
at this hour of the night?
note: leading space: follows #3715 directly on the same line

en: Ah! Don't tell me
You've come here after me, haven't you!
So it really was me, not the Public Hall,
that you were curious about.
Don't misunderstand me!
It's true that I came here after you, but
it's certainly not because I like men!
Then just what is it
you're "after" from me?
(Uh-oh...)
(Oh, well,
note: followed by a pause (space added automatically), #3728, dots and #1263 ')'

en: now that it's come to this
Josef!
note: shared: 'Josef! / The truth is...' and msg 142198 'Wait! / Josef!'

en: The truth is, I've always liked you!
Waaah, stop it!
Wait!
, if that is my master's command
I shall go wherever you wish
note: followed by '...' (#2) + '.' (#25): needs #25 variant '' for msg 143994 to avoid four dots

en: I am Wesseli.
I'm a trader.
My work keeps me extremely busy,
so I'm afraid I've no time to talk with you.
, what a pleasure.
If there's anything you need,
please don't hesitate to ask.
Do come by the trading house again.
I am Wesseli, a trader.
Being a trader
keeps a man rather busy, you know.
If you'll excuse me.
How have you been lately?
I thought I'd come home and see my wife's
face for once.
I am the master of this house,
Wesseli the trader.
Pardon me, did we have an appointment?
No, this is my first visit.
I make it a rule never to see
anyone without an appointment.
My time is precious. Good day.
Sorry, but if you have business with me,
please come to the trading house by day.
If all I get when I do come home is
